items.title: J. Leo Rayhill interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 23, 2007
items.q: Yeah. Fletcher Henderson and all those folks.

ctx.x: Yeah. There were some wonderful ones.
Yeah. Fletcher Henderson and all those folks.

Oh yeah. There was one, there’s a legend of a big band arranger who had made a wonderful new arrangement for Harry James. And Harry and Count Basie were big time friends. And Harry says, “I want you to come and hear my band,” when the Count had a night off. So he comes and he listens to this arrangement, and it’s by Jimmy Mundy, the arranger, and it was the same one that he sold Count Basie. It was very funny.
